- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for downward surprise.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model overcorrects in next 3–5 days; reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.  
- If true price drops sharply after a peak, model fails to mean-revert; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of prior 10 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates in early days (1–7) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; apply 1–2% downward bias to first 7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.6 → -0.4 → +0.6), model overfits to recent trend; use 3-day sentiment average to smooth forecast.
